title: try_into().unwrap() on verified-length slice in signing.rs
description: signing.rs lines 26 and 53: after explicitly checking bytes.len() != 32, the code calls bytes.try_into().unwrap(). The unwrap() can never panic (the length was just verified), but it is dead code that looks like it could panic. The idiomatic replacement is an already-allocated [u8;32] initialized with copy_from_slice, or TryFrom with .expect(). This is not a runtime hazard but the unwrap masks what the check is for. More critically, if someone removes the len-check guard and the unwrap survives, it panics on malformed input at a key-loading boundary.
